clip_script:
Imagine the same sentence in isiZulu, English and Afrikaans. Different words, same meaning. Fractions, decimals and percentages are like that: three languages for one amount. Half of a pizza is one half, zero comma five and fifty percent, and the pizza does not care which you say.

Here is how to translate. Fraction to decimal: the fraction line is a division sign in disguise. Three eighths means three divided by eight. Do the division — eight into three point zero zero zero — and you get zero comma three seven five. Decimal to percentage: percent means out of a hundred, so ask how many hundredths you have. Zero comma three seven five is thirty-seven and a half hundredths: thirty-seven comma five percent. Three eighths, zero comma three seven five, thirty-seven and a half percent. One amount.
visual_style: A single point on a number line with three labels rotating; a sale tag, a test paper and a measuring jug
